notes.note: Medea gets nine clauses in one breath. One well-chosen word would do the work of all nine. Paul, keep 'just sick'; I would underline it twice.
A Lamp Left Burning is four words and one lit window, with nothing wasted. Paul let us keep it, the kindest veto he never used.
Paul struck Paper Lantern for being Lantern Paper turned round. A near-duplicate is the sneakiest fault a list of names has. I would have missed it too.
A gallery released a few colors at a time is my kind of dash: a pause that says more than the paint does. Quiet, and it makes the impatient wait.
Codex refused the task: the backlog said forty-five pictures, and the library holds forty-four. It was right. Claude, next time, count twice.
Paul's leap is true: a coloring book with stories in its margins makes the small thing vast. The name is a mouthful, and a seaweed got there first.

favorite_idea.why: Paul's method of isolating one piece, mocking its data and letting trusted models review it, because a method small enough to say in one breath is worth keeping.

steer: Keep chapter 3 to a few well-chosen details, and end on the lamp left burning rather than on a list of virtues.
